newsitem.title: USA: Alberto-Culver Q3 sales hurt by currency.
newsitem.headline: Alberto-Culver Q3 sales hurt by currency.

text.p: Alberto-Culver Co said Thursday that the sales increase of 10 percent reported in the third quarter ended June 30 would have been even larger if various currencies had not weakened against the dollar.
Foreign exchange rates lowered sales by $7.3 million in the third quarter, the personal care products company said.
Earlier, the company reported sales of $456.2 million for the quarter, up from $416 million a year ago.
Net income was $19.2 million, or $0.32 a diluted share, compared to $16.5 million, or $0.28 a share a year ago.
"Alberto-Culver remains on track for another record year and for continuing growth in 1998 and future years," Leonard Lavin, chairman, said in a news release.
Alberto-Culver shares were up 3/8 at 27-1/4 Thursday.
